latest_release.name: Zephyr 4.5.0
latest_release.body:
We are pleased to announce the release of Zephyr version 4.5.0.

For a closer look at some of the key additions in this release, check out the [announcement article](https://www.zephyrproject.org/zephyr-4-5-release-blog/) on the Zephyr blog, along with its [companion video](http://zephyrproject.org/zephyr-4.5-video).

Major enhancements with this release include:

## New architectures: Infineon TriCore and Qualcomm Hexagon
Zephyr now supports the [Infineon TriCore architecture](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/boards/index.html#arch=tricore), used in AURIX automotive microcontrollers, and the [Qualcomm Hexagon DSP architecture](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/boards/index.html#arch=hexagon).

## Multimedia Pipeline (mpipe)
The new experimental [Multimedia Pipeline (mpipe)](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/mpipe/index.html#mpipe) subsystem, inspired by GStreamer, provides a framework for building media applications from source, transform and sink elements linked into a zero-copy pipeline.

## Networking enhancements
Optimizations across the IP stack deliver up to 21% higher TCP throughput in the [zperf loopback benchmark](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/samples/net/zperf/README-loopback-icount.html#zperf-loopback-icount).

The networking stack also gains several new features:
- [QUIC](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/connectivity/networking/api/quic.html#quic-transport-interface) and [HTTP/3](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/connectivity/networking/api/http_server.html#http-server-interface) support.
- [RTP](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/connectivity/networking/api/rtp.html#rtp-interface) ([RFC3550](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3550.html)) stack for sending and receiving media streams over UDP.
- [SSH server and client](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/samples/net/ssh/README.html#ssh-server-client), including a shell backend.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP) server](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/connectivity/networking/api/mcp.html#mcp-server-interface) to let AI agents use tools exposed by a device.
- Gateway features: IPv4 forwarding, NAT, IPv6 router role and [DHCPv6](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/connectivity/networking/api/dhcpv6.html#dhcpv6-interface) prefix delegation.

## New driver classes
Zephyr 4.5 adds several new driver APIs:
- [Buzzer](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/buzzer.html#buzzer-api) for passive and active buzzers driven by PWM or GPIO,
- [Clock Monitor](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/clock_monitor.html#clock-monitor-api) for runtime observation of clock frequency,
- [DALI](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/dali.html#dali-api) for the Digital Addressable Lighting Interface,
- [LIN](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/lin.html#lin) for the Local Interconnect Network automotive serial bus,
- [MUX](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/mux.html#mux-api) for hardware signal multiplexers, and
- [Pulse IO](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/pulse_io.html#pulse-io-api) for hardware that generates and captures timed digital edges, as needed by addressable LED strips and infrared transceivers.

## Security and SBOM improvements
This release improves SBOM generation, hardening checks and cryptographic acceleration:
- [SPDX 3 SBOMs](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/west/zephyr-cmds.html#west-spdx) that record how the image was built ([Build profile](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/west/zephyr-cmds.html#west-spdx-build-profile)), the [prebuilt libraries](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/west/zephyr-cmds.html#west-spdx-blobs) it links, and [package identifiers](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/west/zephyr-cmds.html#west-spdx-package-id) for vulnerability matching.
